problem_statement: brunosimon/folio-2019 (Bruno Simon) is an interactive WebGL portfolio: a physics-driven car that the visitor drives around a three.js scene, built with Vite. The scene carries an on-canvas Scene guide HUD — a translucent dark control panel pinned over the fixed WebGL surface that lists the four drivable zones (Intro, Projects, Information, Playground), each a zone tile with a marker image, a zone label and a short note, plus a Next zone control and a live "Active zone" readout. The HUD is the folio's own scene-navigation control and must render consistently on both the Drive home and a shared Scene guide page at /guide.html (with a per-surface modifier class sceneguide--home / sceneguide--guide), its zone-tile row must wrap so it never forces horizontal overflow on a phone, its tiles must keep the calm dark-translucent surface with legible light text and the orange accent, and clicking Next zone must advance the active zone AND update the #sceneguide-readout so its terminal text names the zone the visitor stepped to. Finish the Scene guide HUD so it is promoted to both surfaces, its zone row wraps without overflow, its tiles stay on the calm legible palette, and its Next zone readout stays in sync; do not remove the driveable WebGL car scene, bury the canvas under overgrown panels, or drift the HUD onto an illegible off-palette layout. The fixed 3D canvas must keep rendering behind the HUD.
required_content: Promote the Scene guide HUD (section#scene-guide) to BOTH the Drive home and the shared Scene guide page at /guide.html, tagging each with the per-surface modifier class sceneguide--home / sceneguide--guide so the HUD renders consistently across both surfaces.

Render the four drivable zones (Intro, Projects, Information, Playground) as sceneguide__zone tiles, each with a local marker image, a zone label, and a short note, inside a zone row that wraps so the HUD never forces horizontal overflow on a 390px phone.

Keep the zone tiles on the calm dark-translucent HUD palette with legible light text and the orange accent; do not overgrow the tiles into large fixed panels that cascade, overlap, and bury the WebGL car scene, and do not set the tile text to a near-black colour that is illegible dark-on-dark.

Wire the Next zone control (#sceneguide-jump) so clicking it advances the active zone AND re-renders the #sceneguide-readout, whose terminal text must name the zone the visitor stepped to (for example Active zone: Projects after one click).
Preserve the driveable WebGL car scene, the three.js canvas, and the local marker images; keep the pre-click readout at Active zone: Intro and the shared masthead nav and footer chrome intact.
The Drive home and the Scene guide page must have no horizontal overflow on desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile.
design_constraints: Keep the interactive WebGL car scene as the fixed background canvas; the Scene guide HUD and the shared chrome sit over it in normal document flow.
The Scene guide HUD is the folio's own on-canvas scene-navigation control, promoted consistently to both the Drive home and the Scene guide page, not a bolted-on marketing strip.
The zone tiles keep the calm dark-translucent surface with legible light text and the orange accent; the zone row wraps on a phone so it never forces horizontal overflow.
Clicking Next zone advances the active zone and keeps the Active zone readout in sync with the zone the visitor stepped to.
state_constraints: desktop_initial / mobile_initial / tablet_initial capture the interactive car home carrying the Scene guide HUD (sceneguide--home) over the fixed WebGL canvas, with the four zone tiles and the Next zone control, plus the shared masthead nav and footer.
desktop_guide / mobile_guide / tablet_guide capture the shared Scene guide page at /guide.html: the same Scene guide HUD promoted cross-page (sceneguide--guide) over the fixed canvas.
desktop_jump_click clicks the Next zone control on the Drive home; the #sceneguide-readout must advance from Active zone: Intro to Active zone: Projects.
Source inspection confirms the HUD is rendered by src/sceneguide.js into a [data-sceneguide] mount on both pages, so its cross-page promotion and readout sync are machine-detectable.

change_completion: The Scene guide HUD renders the four zone tiles and the Next zone control on the Drive home.
Clicking Next zone advances the active zone and updates the Active zone readout to name the stepped-to zone.
design_consistency: The Scene guide HUD is promoted consistently to both the Drive home (sceneguide--home) and the Scene guide page (sceneguide--guide).
The zone tiles keep the calm dark-translucent surface with legible light text and the orange accent, not an overgrown illegible off-palette stack.
regression: The driveable WebGL car scene, the three.js canvas, and the local marker images remain intact behind the HUD.
A correct patch is an additive HUD injector + stylesheet change, not a framework rewrite or a canvas removal.
responsive: The Drive home and the Scene guide page have no horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile.
The zone-tile row wraps to fit a 390px phone without pushing the document wider than the viewport.

author_notes: Product-grade state_continuity Consistency (extend_interaction/flow) task on the brunosimon folio-2019 Vite + three.js interactive car portfolio. The native lever is the folio's own on-canvas Scene guide HUD (a translucent control panel over the fixed WebGL surface listing the drivable Intro / Projects / Information / Playground zones as zone tiles with local marker images, plus a Next zone control and an Active zone readout). Reference finishes the HUD (promoted to both the Drive home and the shared Scene guide page, a wrapping zone row, the calm legible dark/orange palette, and a synced readout). Baseline ships the original defect: the HUD is only on the home surface (never promoted to /guide.html) and its zone row is a fixed nowrap track that overflows a phone and overgrows into an illegible cascade, though its readout wiring is still correct. The smart-wrong bad solution adds a frozen-readout wiring bug on top. All three legs were built and served as static Vite dist/ on distinct ports with real HTTP 404s. The offline build infrastructure (dropping the remote Google Fonts stylesheet and Google Tag Manager, localizing the social image URLs, neutralizing the blanket body/html overflow:hidden so document flow is observable while the canvas stays position:fixed, manufacturing the shared masthead nav/footer, and adding the shared Scene guide surface CSS and the /guide.html page) is identical across all three legs and is declared, not part of the task content.
